text.p: These are the leading stories in the Belgrade press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
NASA BORBA
- U.S. agrees to deblock five Montgenegrin cargo vessels impounded in its ports since the end of May 1992.

- President of the Parliamentary party of Kosovo Adem Demaqi informs Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) that Kosovo Albanians cannot accept its recommendations because it treats them as a national minority and accepts "Serbian agression in Kosovo."
- There can be no free elections in Serbia without free media, says former Yugoslav prime minister Milan Panic in a letter to Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic.
- Independent media and opposition parites criticise the new draft information law saying it ensures monopoly of state media.

- Money supply in February down by 90 million dinars on January dropping to 5.27 billion dinars from 5.36 and lower in the first two months of 1997 than at the end of last year when it reached up to 5.5 billion dinars, says independent news agency Beta.
- Independent trade union of Serbian farmers says it will block roads in Serbia if government does not pay all purchased crops and write off due taxes by March 30.

- Bosnian Serb Prime Minister Gojko Klickovic criticises the Hague war crimes tribunal for failure to include the charge of crimes against humanity in its indictment of four people accused of crimes against Bosnian Serbs.

- Acting Belgrade University Rector Tomislav Dragovic says the university school year will last until September 30 and the 1997/98 school year will start on October 1 to permit students to make up classess missed during three months of protests.
POLITIKA
- Bosnian Serb government accepts bill on ratification of the special ties agreement between Yugoslavia and Bosnian Serb republic.

- Production capacties of Serbian power company EPS thermoelectric power plants are dropping, the plants produced 11 billion Kwhs this winter season which is four billion Kwhs less than seven years earlier and decrease of production expected to continue in next five years, say economists.
- Exports grew by 48.9 percent in the first two months of 1997 in relation to the same period last year, according to federal statistics.
- The two chambers of the Yugoslav parliament will elect the new federal government at their March 20 session.
VECERNJE NOVOSTI
- Pensions for January will be reduced by 12.8 percent, the amount that earnings were reduced under the new way of statistically counting wages.
- Problem related to Yugoslavia's membership in the International Monetary Fund is political and not economic, says head of Yugoslav team for negotiations with the organisation Oskar Kovac.
BORBA
- Serbian postal company PTT to employ domestic industry in its development programme for which it plans to spend 2.6 billion dinars ($472 million) this year.
BLIC

- Confusion at Belgrade university, classes resume but students continue their protest marches waiting for rector's resignation to be officially recognised by the university council session slated for March 20. -- Belgrade newsroom +381 11 2224305
